name: The fixed round to purity (Ājīvika, as reported)

stages.name: kaṇhābhijāti
stages.description: butchers, hunters, bandits and all of cruel livelihood (AN 6.57)

stages.name: nīlābhijāti
stages.description: mendicants who live 'by thorns' and teachers of deeds

stages.name: haliddābhijāti
stages.description: white-clothed lay followers of naked ascetics

stages.name: paramasukkābhijāti
stages.description: Nanda Vaccha, Kisa Saṅkicca, Makkhali Gosāla; in the Tamil report, the birth in which release is reached

stages.name: dukkhass' anta
stages.description: reached by fool and wise alike after 8,400,000 great aeons, like a ball of string run out; not hastened by vows or austerity

notes: Reported by opponents only. It is a fixed course that every being runs, not a path of practice; the classes are grades of beings. Bands are assigned only to the culmination (B7); the earlier classes are left unbanded because the doctrine denies that effort moves one along them.

name: The eight stages of a person (aṭṭha purisabhūmiyo)
notes: DN 2 only names 'eight stages of a person'; the stage names and glosses are Buddhaghosa's, recalled with low confidence. A life-cycle list rather than a path of practice.
